A Night at the Airport: 转机航班延误,作者在机场度过漫长一夜,却在陌生旅客身上收获了温暖。

My connecting flight from Helsinki to Manchester was supposed to leave at 21:40. At 20:15, the departure board changed without warning: the flight was delayed until 06:00 the next morning. Around me, families sank into their seats, and a long queue of angry passengers formed at the service desk within minutes.

The airline offered meal vouchers, but no hotel, because the delay was caused by weather. I found a row of seats near a closed cafe, wrapped my coat around myself, and prepared for a long night. The terminal lights stayed on all night, and every hour an announcement reminded us to keep our belongings with us.

At about two in the morning, a woman sitting opposite offered me a mint and asked where I was heading. Her name was Anni, a nurse returning from a conference. We talked quietly about our homes, bad airport coffee and the books on our phones. Two other stranded travellers joined in, and someone shared a portable charger like it was treasure.

At dawn we boarded, red-eyed but calm. When we landed, Anni waved goodbye and said, "Not the worst night, in the end." She was right. The delay stole my sleep, but it gave me something rarer: proof that strangers can turn a hard night into a good memory.
